title: Reading a price graph without guessing
target: How to use the price graph in TCG Card Shop Simulator: what the screen can show, how the line and its colours are drawn, what the lists of prices and days are for, and how a graded card gets a price of its own.
version: no version stated by this build (see the sources page)
prerequisites: Enough history for a line to mean something

steps.do: Open the price graph rather than guessing a price, because the game has a screen for an item's price over time.
steps.because: there is a screen dedicated to an item's price over time (ItemPriceGraphScreen)

steps.do: Know that the same screen serves goods and cards, because it carries groups for both.
steps.because: the screen has an item group and a card group beside its value group (m_ItemGrp, m_CardGrp, m_ValueGrp)

steps.do: Read what the screen says it is showing, because it names the item, the card and the card's grade.
steps.because: the screen carries an item name, a card name and a card grade name (m_ItemName, m_CardName, m_CardGradeName)

steps.do: Expect the line to be worked out at run time rather than baked, because its start and end positions are calculated.
steps.because: the graph has a start and an end point, each calculated into a position (m_GraphStartXY, m_GraphEndXY, m_GraphStartCalculatePos, m_GraphEndCalculatePos)

steps.do: Give the line a moment, because it is drawn with a speed and a divider rather than appearing all at once.
steps.because: the line has a lerp speed and a divider of its own (m_LineGraphLerpSpeed, m_LineGraphDivide)

steps.do: Read the colour as the answer, because the graph keeps a positive, a negative and a neutral colour.
steps.because: the graph has a positive, a negative and a neutral colour (m_PositiveColor, m_NegativeColor, m_NeutralColor)

steps.do: Look at the lists behind the picture rather than only the line, because the prices and the days are kept as lists.
steps.because: the graph keeps lists of price lines, dots, price texts and day texts (m_ItemPriceLineGrpList, m_DotSpriteList, m_PriceTextList, m_DayTextList)

steps.do: Check a graded card on its own line, because the screen keeps a quick-view price for graded cards.
steps.because: the screen keeps a quick-view price text for graded cards (m_QuickViewGradedCardPriceTextList)

steps.do: Switch the grade from the screen when the grade is what you are comparing.
steps.because: the screen has a change-grade option screen and a list of change-grade buttons (m_ChangeGradeOptionUIScreen, m_ChangeGradeBtnList)

steps.do: Remember that the tag on the shelf is a separate thing, because floor price tags are objects of their own.
steps.because: price tags on the floor are objects of their own (InteractablePriceTag, UI_PriceTag)

commonMistakes: Guessing a price when the screen would have shown the history.
Reading a card's line as if it were a shelf item's, when the screen keeps the two groups apart.
Ignoring the colour and reading only the shape of the line.
Forgetting that a graded card has a price of its own on the screen.
Setting the shelf tag and expecting the graph to change on its own.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Identifiers are listed on the technical reference pages; nothing here is estimated.
